record_identity.title: Dixell refrigeration-control compromises at French supermarkets on 12–13 October 2026

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Dixell refrigeration-control compromises at French supermarkets on 12–13 October 2026
incident_identity.date_basis: Le Monde reports another overnight refrigeration-controller incident, 12–13 October 2026, involving Dixell-controlled sites, following the 11–12 October Danfoss occurrence.

summary: During the night of 12–13 October 2026, French supermarkets operating Dixell refrigeration management equipment experienced unauthorised changes to cooling and defrost settings. A refrigeration technician reported that a Bordeaux-area store detected abnormal temperatures and intervened before losing stock. At an E.Leclerc store in Lescure-d'Albigeois, refrigerated stock was discarded after the cold chain was disrupted. A technician reported very rapid parameter changes, including a freezer setting changed from −22°C to 150°C; this was a reported setpoint value, not a measured cabinet temperature. CERT-FR added Dixell XWEB and Copeland XWEB to its wider refrigeration-security alert. Neither a common operator with the previous night's Danfoss events nor an initial access mechanism has been established.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Le Monde reports a distinct overnight 12–13 October wave at Dixell-managed stores, with contrasting site outcomes: a Bordeaux-area store avoided stock loss after detection and intervention, while an E.Leclerc in the Tarn discarded refrigerated inventory. A quoted refrigeration specialist inferred automation from a rate of two or three parameter changes per second. The reported 150°C value describes a setting, not verified physical heating to that temperature. CERT-FR expanded its national alert to Dixell XWEB and Copeland XWEB but did not identify a shared perpetrator, exploit or fleet-management origin. The evidence does not establish AI-assisted development, formal fuzz testing or a defensive test triggered by the earlier Danfoss event.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: Unauthorised changes to live Dixell-managed refrigeration controls were associated with disrupted cold storage and discarded inventory at one reported store. At another, detection and intervention prevented stock loss. The technical command source and operator are unknown, and the later timing does not prove a common campaign with Danfoss. This is a separately bounded cyber-physical context occurrence, not a finding that an AI system conducted tests or caused damage.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The separate episode permits assessment of material refrigeration disruption alongside a documented site-level containment response. Its proximity to the earlier Danfoss event is a research lead, not evidence of a shared operator, AI model or unsafe defensive-testing workflow.
assessment_boundaries: No independent evidence attributes the Dixell compromise to AI, autonomous agents, generated testing code, fuzzing, Mistral, Astra or another named model.
A technician inferred automation from rapid parameter updates; no underlying execution trace or testing sequence has been published.
The 150°C figure is a reported configuration setting, not a measured freezer temperature.
One Bordeaux-area store reportedly avoided food loss after intervention; this positive outcome must not be conflated with the stock loss at the Tarn store.
The same operator, platform, maintenance contractor or command origin has not been proven across the two nights.
CERT-FR's inclusion of Copeland XWEB in the wider alert does not establish that every Copeland installation shared the reported Dixell occurrence.
The first wave's national store counts and approximately US$112,000 Intermarché loss are not assigned to this occurrence.
No quantified Dixell-wave financial loss or physical injury is established by the preserved sources.
The non-AI context admission is authorised by the maintainer; no class-level taxonomy or AI mechanism finding has been completed.
